findings.message: Acceptance 1 requires a test proving a schema-1 document raises ResultsInvalid. Every schema-1 case in test_invalid_results is also invalid for another reason: an `error` outcome, a blank node ID, an extra key, or a list for `tests`. Under the old reader, which accepted schema 1, each of these was still refused. So the suite passes even if schema 1 were still accepted.
findings.paved_road: Add a schema-1 case to the refused parametrize list that is otherwise valid, such as {"schema_version": 1, "tests": {"test_a": "passed"}}.

findings.message: The ticket says a schema-1 document joins the refused cases here. The only schema-1 cases in test_invalid_results also fail the old reader for other reasons: they have a `seconds` key, a list for `tests`, a blank node ID, or an `error` outcome. Accepting a valid schema-1 document would therefore go undetected.

check() chooses its value with `repository if name == "repository" else percent(paths)`, so it decides by the check name and ignores the paths it was given. A gate package key `repository`, or a file at the repository root named `repository`, gets the repository-wide percent instead of its own, so evaluate's results change. evaluate also re-implements the covered/total formula in a local percent() instead of using what percentages returns. That is a second copy of the formula that can drift.
findings.paved_road: Pass the repository value into the repository check explicitly. For example, pass the value instead of paths, or use percentages()' per-file map for file checks and compute only package aggregates locally. Never branch on the check name.

findings.message: The section 12 `chupa.testreport` bullet still says "The results reader accepts schemas 1 and 2; schema 2 also contains a matching `seconds` map of finite nonnegative floats." The reader now refuses schema 1.
findings.paved_road: Change the sentence to say the reader accepts only schema 2 and refuses schema 1.
